                    text: [32m'# Function: apiNamespace() - Wasp\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-08-11, [Read more](https://wasp.sh/docs/0.24/api/@wasp.sh/spec/functions/apiNamespace)\n'[39m +

                    text: [32m'# Wasp now lets you write your full-stack logic as a spec in TypeScript\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2026-06-15, last updated: 2026-08-14, [Read more](https://wasp.sh/blog/2026/06/15/wasp-typescript-spec)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'You write the Wasp TypeScript Spec (TS Spec) in `*.wasp.ts` files by constructing the `app` spec object.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'You do so by using the spec constructors from `@wasp.sh/spec`: `page`, `route`, `query`, `job`, `api`, … . That is your "vocabulary" that you use to specify the parts of your web app, and then compose them all together into one big `app` spec object.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { app, page, query, route } from "@wasp.sh/spec";\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { MainPage } from "./src/MainPage" with { type: "ref" }; // React\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The only thing Wasp requires from you is that you export an `app` spec object from the `main.wasp.ts` file.'[39m

                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Wasp moves from custom DSL to TypeScript spec and rebrands in Launch Week #12\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2026-07-21, last updated: 2026-07-21, [Read more](https://reasoncore.dev/post/wasp-moves-from-custom-dsl-to-typescript-spec-and-rebrands-in-launch-week-12)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The release adds server-side prerendering, updated docs and migration guides, and a TypeScript spec API via @wasp.sh/spec.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- TS Spec uses a canonical main.wasp.ts in the project root with imports from "@wasp.sh/spec" and examples showing wasp: { version: "^0.24.0" }.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'TS Spec replaces the separate DSL file (main.wasp) and the older TS Config style with a TypeScript-native spec file named main.wasp.ts in the project root.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The canonical imports are provided from the @wasp.sh/spec package.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The canonical import line shown in the docs is:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { app, page, query, route } from "@wasp.sh/spec"\n'[39m +

                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The immediate, concrete changes for developers are visible in three places: the canonical file name (main.wasp.ts at the project root), the @wasp.sh/spec API surface (app, page, query, route, job, api, etc.), and migration guides in the docs for moving from the old DSL and earlier config styles.'[39m
                  },

                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Actions | Wasp\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-08-11, [Read more](https://wasp.sh/docs/data-model/operations/actions)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'To create an Action in Wasp, we begin with an\n'[39m +
                      [32m'…\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { action, app } from "@wasp.sh/spec"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { createTask, markTaskAsDone } from "./src/actions" with { type: "ref" }\n'[39m +

                      [32m'// ...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'spec: [\n'[39m +

                      [32m'action(markTaskAsDone),\n'[39m +
                      [32m'],\n'[39m +
                      [32m'})\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'To call an Action on the client, you can import it from\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'wasp/client/operations\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'and call it directly.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Declaring an Action enables you to import and use it anywhere in your code (on the server or the client).\n'[39m +

                    text: [32m"# Wasp's Programmable Spec Lets You Build File-Based Routing in 45 Lines\n"[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2026-07-24, last updated: 2026-07-24, [Read more](https://www.devdigest.org/articles/wasps-programmable-spec-lets-you-build-file-based-routing-in-45-lines)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +

                      [32m'import { globSync } from &#34;node:fs&#34;;\n'[39m +

                value: [
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Interface: Api | Wasp\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-08-12, [Read more](https://wasp.sh/docs/api/@wasp.sh/spec/interfaces/Api)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'A custom HTTP endpoint mounted on the Wasp server.\n'[39m +

                      [32m'Unlike operations, APIs are plain Express handlers that receive `req`,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`res`, and a Wasp `context`.\n'[39m +

                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Interface: Server | Wasp\n'[39m +

                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { myMiddlewareConfigFn, mySetupFunction } from "./src/myServerSetupCode" with { type: "ref" }\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Async function called once on server start.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Wasp awaits it before the\n'[39m +
                      [32m'server accepts requests.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Receives a context containing the Express `app`\n'[39m +
                      [32m'and underlying `http.Server`, so you can register custom routes, set up\n'[39m +
                      [32m'additional databases or WebSockets, or kick off scheduled jobs.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'In TypeScript, you can type the function with the `ServerSetupFn` type\n'[39m +

                      [32m'#### Example ​\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { type ServerSetupFn } from "wasp/server"\n'[39m +

                      [32m'await setUpSomeResource()\n'[39m +

                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-04-14, [Read more](https://contextqmd.com/libraries/wasp/versions/0.22.0/pages/web/docs/project/server-config)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'You can configure the behavior of the server via the `server` field of `app` declaration:\n'[39m +

                      [32m'This function is expected to be async and will be awaited before the server starts accepting any requests.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The `setupFn` function receives the `express.Application` and the `http.Server` instances as part of its context.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +

                      [32m'}'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Add `app` and `server` to server `setupFn` by shayneczyzewski · Pull Request #1017 · wasp-lang/wasp\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2023-02-15, last updated: 2026-04-16, [Read more](https://github.com/wasp-lang/wasp/pull/1017)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This PR adds `app` and `server` to the server `setupFn`, mainly as an escape hatch.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Users can then do arbitrary Express endpoints, or things like websockets.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'I would recommend adding a type for the `ServerSetupFn` like:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'type ServerSetupFn = (context: ServerSetupFnContext) => void;\n'[39m +
                      [32m'type ServerSetupFnContext = {\n'[39m +

                      [32m'server: http.Server,\n'[39m +

                      [32m"which the user can import like `import { ServerSetupFnContext } from '@wasp/types';` or similar.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'| | |export type Application = express.Application|\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'| | |export type Server = http.Server|\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'For example, see `function addCustomRoute(app: Application)` in `serverSetup.ts`.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +

                      [32m"import { Application } from 'express';\n"[39m +
                      [32m"import { Server } from 'http';\n"[39m +
                      [32m'export type ServerSetupFn = (context: ServerSetupFnContext) => Promise<void>\n'[39m +
                      [32m'export type ServerSetupFnContext = {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'app: Application,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'server: Server,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m"export { Application } from 'express';\n"[39m +
                      [32m"export { Server } from 'http';\n"[39m +
                      [32m'```'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Custom HTTP API Endpoints - Wasp\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-08-11, [Read more](https://wasp.sh/docs/advanced/apis)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'APIs are used to tie a JS function to a certain endpoint e.g.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'To create a Wasp API, you must:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'1. Declare the API in Wasp using the\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'api\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'constructor\n'[39m +
                      [32m"2. Define the API's NodeJS implementation\n"[39m +
                      [32m"After completing these two steps, you'll be able to call the API from the client code (via our\n"[39m +
                      [32m'…\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'First, we need to declare the API in the Wasp file and you can easily do this with the\n'[39m +
                      [32m'…\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'spec: [\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'To make sure the Wasp compiler generates the types for APIs for use in the NodeJS implementation, you should add your\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'api\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m's to your Wasp file first *and* keep the\n'[39m +
                      [32m'…\n'[39m +

                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Configuring Middleware - Wasp framework\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-08-13, [Read more](https://wasp.sh/docs/0.14/advanced/middleware-config)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Wasp comes with a minimal set of useful Express middleware in every application.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Wasp's Express server has the following middleware by default:\n"[39m +

                    text: [32m'# Package — web - Alfred Black - What is Alfred Black?\n'[39m +

                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`packages/web/` is the **dashboard** — a [Wasp](https://wasp.sh) framework\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Everything declarative — routes, queries, actions, jobs, entities, auth\n'[39m +

                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Wasp: The Batteries-Included Full-Stack Framework That Writes Its ...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2026-06-13, last updated: 2026-08-11, [Read more](https://reactlibs.dev/articles/wasp/)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"It's a Rails-like, batteries-included framework for JavaScript and TypeScript that lets you describe the high-level shape of your app — its routes, pages, auth methods, data operations, and jobs — in one concise spec, and then leans on a real compiler to generate all the glue code between **React**, **Node.js/Express**, and **Prisma**.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'You write the business logic; Wasp writes the plumbing: routing, the RPC layer, auth flows, type definitions, cache invalidation, and deployment config.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- **Operations (Queries and Actions)** — a zero-API RPC layer that lets the client call server functions like local functions, fully type-safe, with no REST or GraphQL boilerplate.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- **Full-stack type safety** — types flow from your Prisma model through the server operation and into your React component automatically.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Operations are plain Node.js functions that run on the server but are invoked from the client as if they were local.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'You never define a REST endpoint or a GraphQL resolver.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Because of full-stack type safety, a query that returns `Recipe[]` makes the data typed as `Recipe[]` in your component with zero manual typing.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'You write the server function:'[39m

                    text: [32m'# https://wasp.sh/llms-full.txt\n'[39m +

                      [32m'|\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Currently, Wasp only has support for one job executor, `PgBoss`.\n'[39m +

                    text: [32m'# Function: job()\n'[39m +

                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'> **job**(`fn`, `config`): `Job`\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Creates a Job definition.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Jobs are background tasks that persist across server restarts, can be\n'[39m +

                      [32m'`"PgBoss"`\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Executor backing this job.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Currently only `"PgBoss"` is available.\n'[39m +

                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +

                  },

                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Jobs | pg-boss\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-08-14, [Read more](https://pgboss.io/api/jobs)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Creates a new job and returns the job id.\n'[39m +

                      [32m'Finds jobs in a queue by id, singleton key, and/or data.\n'[39m +

                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Background Jobs | wasp-lang/vibe-coding-video | DeepWiki\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2025-11-10, last updated: 2026-07-23, [Read more](https://deepwiki.com/wasp-lang/vibe-coding-video/8.1-background-jobs)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Background jobs in Wasp leverage the PgBoss job queue system, which uses PostgreSQL as the underlying storage and coordination mechanism.\n'[39m +

                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'PgBoss is a job queue built on PostgreSQL.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'When combined with PgBoss, Wasp provides:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- **Declarative job definitions** – define jobs directly in your Wasp config.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +

                      [32m'action scheduleEmailSummary {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'fn: import { scheduleSummaryEmail } from "@src/matches/operations",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'entities: [Match]\n'[39m +

                      [32m'job sendEmailSummaryJob {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'executor: PgBoss,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'perform: {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'fn: import { sendEmailSummary } from "@src/workers/schedule",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'},\n'[39m +
                      [32m'entities: [Match]\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The `sendEmailSummary` job retrieves matches, converts the results into a human-readable format, and delivers the email through Mailgun.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m"As you can see above, the `sendAt` variable determines the job's execution time.\n"[39m +

                      [32m'- Use `cron` for recurring schedules.'[39m

                      [32m'- Wasp Operations (queries/actions) are designed to be called as RPCs from the frontend via wasp/client/operations, not from custom HTTP APIs.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'You can import and call them on the client or server code paths, but using them as regular HTTP endpoints isn’t a supported/stable pattern.\n'[39m +

                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Automatic CRUD | Wasp\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2025-01-09, last updated: 2025-02-10, [Read more](https://wasp-lang.dev/docs/data-model/crud)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +

                      [32m'...\n'[39m +

                      [32m'The overrides are functions that take the following arguments:\n'[39m +

                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Leveraging Wasp for full-stack development - LogRocket Blog\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2024-05-27, last updated: 2026-08-15, [Read more](https://blog.logrocket.com/leveraging-wasp-full-stack-development/)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Wasp, or Web Application Specification, is a declarative full-stack framework introduced in 2020 with the primary goal of addressing the complexities inherent in modern web development.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'To set up the schema for your database, you have to make use of Wasp Entities.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Entities are how you define where data gets stored in your database.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This is usually done using the Prisma Schema Language (PSL) and is defined between the `{=psl psl=}` tags.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'In your `main.wasp` file, add the following code:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'entity Note {=psl\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'title String\n'[39m +
                      [32m'description String\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'export const getNotes = async (args, context) => {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'return context.entities.Note.findMany({\n'[39m +
                      [32m"orderBy: { id: 'asc' },\n"[39m +
                      [32m'});\n'[39m +
                      [32m'};\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'export const createNote = async (args, context) => {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'return context.entities.Note.create({\n'[39m +
                      [32m'data: { title: args.title, description: args.description },\n'[39m +
                      [32m'});\n'[39m +
                      [32m'};\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This function `createNote` takes in two arguments: `args` and `context`, and creates a new note in the database with the given title and description, which are extracted from the `args` object.'[39m

                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Building a PDF Ingestion Pipeline with TypeScript, Wasp, and AI OCR\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2025-12-24, last updated: 2026-02-14, [Read more](https://dev.to/steravy/building-a-pdf-ingestion-pipeline-with-typescript-wasp-and-ai-ocr-1lpp)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Wasp is a declarative DSL that generates React + Node.js + Prisma applications.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +

                content: [32m'import { rollupMetrics } from "wasp/server/jobs";\n'[39m +
                  [32m'\n'[39m +
                  [32m'export const ingestSample = async (req: any, res: any, context: any) => {\n'[39m +

                  [32m'\n'[39m +

                  [32m'    }\n'[39m +
                  [32m'\n'[39m +
                  [32m"    if (!recordedAt || typeof recordedAt !== 'string' || isNaN(Date.parse(recordedAt))) {\n"[39m +
                  [32m'      return res.status(400).json({ error: "recordedAt is missing or is not a parsable ISO-8601 timestamp" });\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    }\n'[39m +
                  [32m'\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    // First, check if a sample with this idempotencyKey already exists\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    const existingSample = await context.entities.Sample.findUnique({\n'[39m +
                  [32m'      where: { idempotencyKey }\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    });\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    if (existingSample) {\n'[39m +
                  [32m'      return res.status(200).json({ id: existingSample.id, duplicate: true });\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    }\n'[39m +
                  [32m'\n'[39m +

                  [32m'\n'[39m +
                  [32m'        const currentWindowSamples = samples.filter((s: any) => {\n'[39m +
                  [32m'          const t = new Date(s.recordedAt).getTime();\n'[39m +
                  [32m'          return t > T_ms - 3600 * 1000 && t <= T_ms;\n'[39m +
                  [32m'        });\n'[39m +
                  [32m'\n'[39m +
                  [32m'        const previousWindowSamples = samples.filter((s: any) => {\n'[39m +
                  [32m'          const t = new Date(s.recordedAt).getTime();\n'[39m +
                  [32m'          return t > T_ms - 7200 * 1000 && t <= T_ms - 3600 * 1000;\n'[39m +
                  [32m'        });\n'[39m +
                  [32m'\n'[39m +
                  [32m'        count = currentWindowSamples.length;\n'[39m +
                  [32m'\n'[39m +
                  [32m'        if (count > 0) {\n'[39m +
                  [32m'          const sum = currentWindowSamples.reduce((acc: number, s: any) => acc + s.value, 0);\n'[39m +
                  [32m'          avg = roundTo3(sum / count);\n'[39m +
                  [32m'\n'[39m +
                  [32m'          const sortedCurrentVals = currentWindowSamples.map((s: any) => s.value).sort((a: number, b: number) => a - b);\n'[39m +
                  [32m'          const pos1 = Math.ceil(0.95 * count);\n'[39m +
                  [32m'          const currentP95 = sortedCurrentVals[pos1 - 1];\n'[39m +
                  [32m'          p95 = currentP95;\n'[39m +
                  [32m'\n'[39m +
                  [32m'          if (previousWindowSamples.length > 0) {\n'[39m +
                  [32m'            const prevCount = previousWindowSamples.length;\n'[39m +
                  [32m'            const sortedPrevVals = previousWindowSamples.map((s: any) => s.value).sort((a: number, b: number) => a - b);\n'[39m +
                  [32m'            const prevPos1 = Math.ceil(0.95 * prevCount);\n'[39m +
                  [32m'            const prevP95 = sortedPrevVals[prevPos1 - 1];\n'[39m +
                  [32m'            delta = roundTo3(currentP95 - prevP95);\n'[39m +
                  [32m'          }\n'[39m +
                  [32m'        }\n'[39m +
                  [32m'      }\n'[39m +
                  [32m'\n'[39m +
                  [32m'      await context.entities.MetricRollup.upsert({\n'[39m +
                  [32m'        where: { metric },\n'[39m +
                  [32m'        update: {\n'[39m +
                  [32m'          count,\n'[39m +
                  [32m'          p95,\n'[39m +
                  [32m'          avg,\n'[39m +
                  [32m'          delta,\n'[39m +
                  [32m'          updatedAt: now,\n'[39m +
                  [32m'        },\n'[39m +
                  [32m'        create: {\n'[39m +
                  [32m'          metric,\n'[39m +
                  [32m'          count,\n'[39m +
                  [32m'          p95,\n'[39m +
                  [32m'          avg,\n'[39m +
                  [32m'          delta,\n'[39m +
                  [32m'          updatedAt: now,\n'[39m +
                  [32m'        }\n'[39m +
                  [32m'      });\n'[39m +
                  [32m'\n'[39m +
                  [32m'      console.log(`[rollupMetrics] Persisted rollup for ${metric}: count=${count}, avg=${avg}, p95=${p95}, delta=${delta}`);\n'[39m +

                  [32m'  }\n'[39m +

                  [32m'};\n'[39m +

                      [32m'created: 2025-04-02, last updated: 2026-08-12, [Read more](https://wasp.sh/blog/2025/04/02/an-introduction-to-database-migrations)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Once you've written a Prisma schema for your app, you'll need to create a **migration file.** This file will contain SQL commands needed to update your database, such as creating new tables or modifying existing ones, or adding database indexes, etc.\n"[39m +
                      [32m"Let's run `wasp db migrate-dev` which uses the Prisma CLI in the background and you'll get the following code in the `migrations/` dir:\n"[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m"When you deploy a Wasp app, the server app's `Dockerfile` runs a Prisma command that applies any migrations you have in the `migrations` dir that are not yet applied.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'This is great!\n'[39m +
                      [32m'As you deploy your code changes, the database changes are also deployed.\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Let's deploy our app to Fly using Wasp's one-line deploy command `wasp deploy fly launch` and we are live at: https://tennis-score-app-client.fly.dev/\n"[39m +

                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Running `wasp db migrate-dev` gives us this migration file:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'-- AlterTable\n'[39m +

                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### Creating migrations ​\n'[39m +
                      [32m'After you made a change in the Prisma schema, you can create a migration by running the following command:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'wasp db migrate-dev\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This command will create a new migration in the `migrations` directory.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The migration is a set of SQL commands that describe the change you made in the schema.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'**In development**, the migrations are applied as soon as you run the `wasp start` command.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'**In production**, the server app first checks if there are any new migrations that need to be applied, and if there are, it applies them before starting the server.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This way, the database schema is always in sync with the Prisma schema.\n'[39m +

                      [32m"In development, when you make changes to your Prisma schema (like renaming a field), Wasp uses Prisma's\n"[39m +

          description: [32m'Executes a given bash command in a persistent shell session with optional timeout, ensuring proper handling and security measures.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations like git, npm, docker, etc. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Before executing the command, please follow these steps:\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'1. Directory Verification:\n'[39m +
            [32m'   - If the command will create new directories or files, first use listFiles to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'2. Command Execution:\n'[39m +
            [32m'   - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes (e.g., cd "path with spaces/file.txt")\n'[39m +
            [32m'   - Examples of proper quoting:\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Usage notes:\n'[39m +

            [32m'# Committing changes with git\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Only create commits when requested by the user. If unclear, ask first. When the user asks you to create a new git commit, follow these steps carefully:\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Git Safety Protocol:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- NEVER update the git config\n'[39m +

            [32m'  - Run a git status command to see all untracked files. IMPORTANT: Never use the -uall flag as it can cause memory issues on large repos.\n'[39m +
            [32m'  - Run a git diff command to see both staged and unstaged changes that will be committed.\n'[39m +
            [32m"  - Run a git log command to see recent commit messages, so that you can follow this repository's commit message style.\n"[39m +
            [32m'2. Analyze all staged changes (both previously staged and newly added) and draft a commit message:\n'[39m +
            [32m'  - Summarize the nature of the changes (eg. new feature, enhancement to an existing feature, bug fix, refactoring, test, docs, etc.). Ensure the message accurately reflects the changes and their purpose (i.e. "add" means a wholly new feature, "update" means an enhancement to an existing feature, "fix" means a bug fix, etc.).\n'[39m +
            [32m'  - Do not commit files that likely contain secrets (.env, credentials.json, etc). Warn the user if they specifically request to commit those files\n'[39m +
            [32m'  - Draft a concise (1-2 sentences) commit message that focuses on the "why" rather than the "what"\n'[39m +
            [32m'  - Ensure it accurately reflects the changes and their purpose\n'[39m +
            [32m'3. You can call multiple tools in a single response. When multiple independent pieces of information are requested and all commands are likely to succeed, run multiple tool calls in parallel for optimal performance. run the following commands:\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'   - Run git status after the commit completes to verify success.\n'[39m +
            [32m'   Note: git status depends on the commit completing, so run it sequentially after the commit.\n'[39m +
            [32m'4. If the commit fails due to pre-commit hook changes, retry the commit ONCE to include these automated changes. If it fails again, it usually means a pre-commit hook is preventing the commit. If the commit succeeds but you notice that files were modified by the pre-commit hook, you MUST amend your commit to include them.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +

            [32m'# Creating pull requests\n'[39m +

            [32m'1. You can call multiple tools in a single response. When multiple independent pieces of information are requested and all commands are likely to succeed, run multiple tool calls in parallel for optimal performance. run the following bash commands in parallel using the executeCommand tool, in order to understand the current state of the branch since it diverged from the main branch:\n'[39m +
